# HOW WE FUND THE NEXT DOUBLING
## A staged capital stack: price first, secured debt second, minority equity only for the money we cannot get back

**Board decision paper | v1.0**
*(Term-sheet drafts, lender term-sheet comparisons and the Gate 0 research brief sit in Annex 1–3 and are not required for this decision.)*

**Decision sought:** approval of (i) the **control floor** in §2 as a binding rule against which every instrument is tested; (ii) the **sequencing principle** in §5 — price, then working-capital debt, then asset-backed capex debt, then equity for irrecoverable spend; (iii) the **funding structure and drawdown order** in §6, with a total committed envelope of €[32]m of which €[14]m is equity; (iv) the **staging gates** in §7 and the **walk-away red lines** in §8; and (v) **€220k (plus €40k contingency) to fund Gate 0**, a six-week verification programme. No instrument is signed and no valuation is accepted at this meeting. The equity price decision becomes irrevocable only at Gate 3.

---

## The recommendation in one paragraph

We are not short of capital in aggregate; we are short of it for about **[20] months**. Base-case cumulative funding gap peaks at €[20]m in month [22] and self-liquidates from FY3 as the capacity we are buying converts to cash — so the correct answer is a **timing structure, not a single raise** (§3.3). We recommend, in this order: **(1) a realised price increase of [4]%** on the constrained order book, which is the cheapest capital available to us — non-dilutive, covenant-free, immediately effective, and it rations scarce capacity toward better customers (§4.1); **(2) customer deposits and capacity-reservation prepayments** of €[4]m against long-lead orders; **(3) a €[10]m borrowing-base revolver** secured on receivables and inventory only, funding working-capital build; **(4) €[14]m of equipment finance** secured on the machines it buys, no all-asset debenture and no personal guarantees; and **(5) €[14]m of minority primary equity in two tranches (€8m + €6m)**, the second at a pre-agreed step-up, used **only** for the irrecoverable spend — hiring, market entry, brand, systems — because that spend has no collateral value and must not be financed with instruments that can foreclose. We reject the framing that this is a valuation dispute: on the arithmetic in §4.4, the difference between the fund's €[110]m and the founders' €[150]m is worth ~[2] points of founder ownership, while a single bad structural term (2× participating preference plus accruing dividend) is worth ~[19]m of founder proceeds at a €[200]m exit. **Price is the small variable; terms are the large one.** We also reject the assumption that debt protects control: a maintenance-covenant bank facility hands a credit committee an effective veto over capex, hiring and acquisitions, and in the stress case in §9 it is the only instrument in this paper that can cost us the company. Two claims here are load-bearing and are therefore **not** asserted: that demand genuinely exceeds capacity at a *higher* price, and that the competitive window is [18–30] months rather than [6]. Gate 0 tests exactly those two, and §7.4 states in advance what result flips the recommendation.

---

## §0 Scope, numbers, and the cost to the core

### 0.1 How to read the figures

| Tag | Type | Example | How certain | Resolved |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **[V]** | **Verifiable fact** | Security law, tax treatment of interest/warrants, statutory consent thresholds, our own audited accounts | Should be *certain* — verify, never estimate | Gate 0, by counsel and auditors |
| **[R]** | **Researchable quantity** | Current market terms for growth debt and minority equity, capex quotes, customer re-qualification cycles, price elasticity | Lender/investor market terms ±[150]bps and structurally variable. **Competitive-window duration: ±[50]% at best** | Gate 0, by CFO + adviser + customer interviews |
| **[D]** | **Design target** | Our leverage cap, dilution floor, growth rate, tranche sizes, price increase | A choice we are making, not a fact we are discovering | Gate 1–3, by this Board |

A number in this paper that is not tagged has not been thought through. **Market norms for terms are [R], not [V]** — nothing in §8 should be treated as "standard" until a term sheet is in front of counsel.

### 0.2 Declared baseline (to be confirmed at Gate 0)

| Item | Figure | Tag |
|---|---|---|
| FY0 revenue | €[60]m | [V] |
| Growth rate achieved | ~[41]% CAGR (doubling every [24] months) | [V] |
| Gross margin | [46]% | [V] |
| EBITDA / margin | €[8.4]m / [14]% | [V] |
| EBITDA→operating cash conversion | [55]% (working-capital build absorbs the rest) | [V] |
| Working capital intensity | [22]% of revenue | [V] |
| Net debt / undrawn facilities | €[4]m / €[3]m | [V] |
| Ownership | Founders [78]%, angels [14]%, ESOP [8]% | [V] |
| Current capacity ceiling | ships €[75]m/yr at full utilisation | [R] |
| Qualified demand / pipeline | €[105]m/yr equivalent | [R] |
| Capex intensity of new capacity | €[0.24] per €1 of annual revenue capacity | [R] |
| Plan: FY1 / FY2 / FY3 revenue | €[84]m / €[118]m / €[160]m | [D] |
| Post-tax incremental ROIC on capacity spend | **[28]%** (§3.4) | [R] |

### 0.3 In scope / out of scope

| In scope | Out |
|---|---|
| Funding the capacity, hiring and market-entry plan to FY3 | Sale of the company; majority recapitalisation |
| Instrument choice, sequencing, staging and red lines | Choice of which new geographies to enter (separate paper) |
| Control architecture (board, reserved matters, exit rights) | Founder estate planning and personal tax |
| Partial founder secondary as a risk-management tool | Any transaction taking founders below the §2 control floor |
| Pricing as a financing instrument | Full pricing-strategy overhaul beyond the constrained book |

### 0.4 The rule of this document

**Every financing option carries a stated cost to the core business**, not only a cost of capital. Diligence consumes the CEO and CFO; covenants consume the finance function monthly; investor boards consume preparation days. These are quantified in §10 and are part of the comparison in §3.5, not a footnote to it.

---

## §1 The three questions that matter

| Wrong question | Right question |
|---|---|
| Debt or equity? | Which *slice* of the requirement are we funding — recoverable assets, self-liquidating working capital, or unrecoverable expansion opex — and what is the correct instrument for that slice? (§3.3) |
| Is the growth fund's valuation fair? | What is the **total structural cost** of their offer — preference, participation, dividend, ratchet, redemption, drag, board — expressed in euros of founder proceeds at three exit values? (§4.4) |
| How do we keep control? | Control is board seats, reserved matters and forced-exit rights, not percentage. Which instrument gives away the most *decision rights* per euro raised? (§2) |

**Corollary 1 — the cheapest capital is a price increase.** If demand exceeds capacity at current prices, our price is below clearing. A [4]% realised increase on the constrained book adds ~€[2.4]m of annual EBITDA **[D]**, is instantly available, dilutes nobody, and reduces the amount of external capital required by roughly €[7]m over the plan. Any financing paper that starts with instruments has skipped its first option.

**Corollary 2 — debt can cost more control than equity.** A minority round at €[110]m pre takes founders from [78]% to ~[69]% and, if structured to the §2 floor, changes no operating decision. A €[24]m all-asset senior facility with a [2.5]× maintenance leverage covenant gives a credit committee a de facto veto on capex, hiring and acquisitions in every quarter where headroom is thin — and in the §9 stress case, the power to enforce. **Dilution is a price; covenant breach is a transfer of the company.**

---

## §2 The control floor (a rule, not a preference)

Founders hold [78]%, comfortably above the [50]% ordinary-resolution and [75]% special-resolution thresholds **[V — confirm for our jurisdiction]**. Percentage is therefore *not* the binding constraint today; decision rights are. The following are binding on management in every negotiation. Any instrument that cannot be structured within them is declined, irrespective of price.

| # | Floor | Threshold |
|---|---|---|
| F1 | Founder economic ownership | never below **[55]%** pre-exit **[D]** |
| F2 | Board |
